newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government's Peasants want to oust premier.
newsitem.headline: Polish government's Peasants want to oust premier.

text.p: The Peasant Party (PSL), junior partner in Poland's left-wing government coalition, said on Tuesday it would seek the dismissal of the prime minister over his agricultural policies.

"The PSL leadership asked the party's parliamentary club to start procedures aimed at a no-confidence vote for the Prime Minister," PSL spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski said, only weeks before scheduled general elections.

But the PSL was unlikely to push through its no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz from the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) because the opposition has said it would not support the proposal.
The Peasants demanded that the government grant farmers advance payments for the 1997 grain harvest, saying this was necessary to stabilise grain prices.
"The lack of clear decisions in that matter by the government causes worries in the countryside," Bentkowski said.

At the last cabinet meeting a week ago, Cimoszewicz refused to discuss the issue, saying the cabinet first needed to see an analysis of the grain market. PSL Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski walked out in protest.
